title: UNION CARBIDE VISIT TO LUSAKA
body:
1. HIGHLIGHT OF UNION CARBIDE OFFICIALS VISIT TO LUSAKA WAS
DINNER WITH PRESIDENT KAUNDA WHO WAS GRACIOUS AND PHILOSO-
PHICAL BUT UNWILLING TO ADDRESS SPECIFICS OF SOUTHERN AFRICAN
DEVELOPMENTS. HE EVADED QUESTIONS DESIGNED TO ELICIT HIS
VIEWS ON FUTURE NAMIBIAN AND RHODESIAN DEVELOPMENT AND GOOD
NATUREDLY BUT FIRMLY REFUSED TO COMMENT ON MALTA TALKS. DESPITE
THIS LACK OF SUBSTANCE, UNION CARBIDE OFFICIALS APPEARED GENUINE-
LY PLEASED TO HAVE HAD THE OPPORTUNITY TO MEET WITH AND SIZE
UP KAUNDA.
2. IN OUR DISCUSSIONS WITH UNION CARBIDE OFFICIALS, WE FOUND
THEM WELL BRIEFED ON RHODESIAN DEVELOPMENTS AND ALERT TO HOW
POSSIBLE SCENARIOS LEADING TO MAJORITY RULE MIGHT AFFECT THEIR
INTERESTS.
3. UNION CARBIDE OFFICIALS WERE DISAPPOINTED IN NOT BEING ABLE
TO MEET WITH NKOMO. EMBASSY AGREED TO TRY TO SET UP AN APPOINT-
MENT WITH HIM IF HE RETURNED TO LUSAKA FOLLOWING MALTA. WE
ARE AIMING FOR FEBRUARY 12.
LOW

title: ANTIDUMPING: UK INVESTIGATION OF DIMETHYLFORMAMIDE IMPORTS
body:
1.  DEPARTMENT OF TRADE AND INDUSTRY (DTI) HAS ADVISED
EMBASSY THAT IT HAS COMPLETED ITS INVESTIGATION OF
ALLEGED DUMPING IN UK OF DIMETHYLFORMAMIDE (DMF) FROM
THE UNITED STATES.  DTI DETERMINED THAT SOME EXPORTS OF
DMF FROM US TO UK HAD IN RECENT MONTHS TAKEN PLACE AT
DUMPED PRICES.  HOWEVER, IN LIGHT OF STATEMENTS BY US
EXPORTER ABOUT FUTURE PRICING POLICY, DTI HAS DECIDED
TAKE NO FURTHER ACTION AT PRESENT.  DTI HAS INFORMED UK
APPLICANTS AND US EXPORTER THAT IT WILL BE PREPARED
REOPEN THE INVESTIGATION IF AT ANY TIME IT RECEIVED
EVIDENCE THAT "DUMPING HAS BEEN RESUMED ON A SCALE SUCH
AS TO CAUSE OR THREATEN TO CAUSE MATERIAL INJURY TO THE
BRITISH INDUSTRY."
2.  DTI HAD PREVIOUSLY FOUND THAT DMF IMPORTS FROM
CANADA HAD NOT BEEN DUMPED.
ANNENBERG

title: JEWISH NEW YEAR IN MOSCOW
body:
1.  NEW YEAR SERVICES AT ARKHIPOV STREET SYNAGOGUE WERE HELD
WITH ONLY ONE MINOR INCIDENT.  POLICE WERE OUT IN FORCE, AND
AS USUAL ON HOLIDAYS DIRECTED TRAFFIC (TAXI TRAFFIC CLEARLY
ORGANIZED) UP ARKHIPOV STREET, MAKING IT DIFFICULT FOR JEWS
TO DANCE IN STREET.  PASSING CAR HIT A YOUNG GIRL WHO WAS
TAKEN TO HOSPITAL.  SITUATION THEN BECAME TENSE AND POLICE
CLOSED STREET TO TRAFFIC BRIEFLY.  THERE WERE NO MAJOR
INCIDENTS SATURDAY MORNING.
2.  FRIDAY EVENING ATTENDANCE WAS ABOUT ONE-THIRD OF 1974.
ATTENDANCE WAS SO TIGHT THAT DOORS REMAINED OPEN UNLIKE LAST
YEAR.  WOMEN'S GALLERY WAS ONLY QUARTER FILLED SINNE TICKETS
WERE DEMANDED AND FEW HAD THEM.  NO MEMBERS OF THE HUMAN
RIGHTS MOVEMENT WERE OBSERVED AT THE SYNAGOGUE UNLIKE
SITUATION IN 1974.
STOESSEL

title: MILITARY ACTIVITY IN BAGHDAD
body:
1.  I SAW KING ON OTHER BUSINESS SHORTLY AFTER NOON JANUARY
29.  KUWAIT CALBE HAD BEEN RECEIVED AND I CONVEYED GENERAL
SENSE OF REPORT IT CONTAINED TO KING.
2.  HE TOLD ME HE HAD JUST RECEIVED A FOLLOW-UP REPORT FROM HIS
MILITARY ATTACHE IN BAGHDAD, WHO INDICATED THAT THERE ARE MORE
MILITARY AND UNIFORMED PARTY PEOPLE ON THE STREETS THAN JORDANIANS
HAD SEEN BEFORE.  THERE WAS ALSO SHOOTING GOING ON SPORADICALLY
AND APPARENTLY NOT VERY FREQUENTLY.  KING MENTIONED PROBLEM OF
SOME SORT NEAR RASHID MILITARY CAMP.  HE ALSO HAD A REPORT
THAT SOME EXECUTIONS MIGHT BE TAKING PLACE AS RESULT OF ACTION
OF PARTY OR MILITARY COURTS AND THAT PROBLEM MAY INVOLVE A
PARTY DISPUTE.  HE SAID HE WOULD LET ME KNOW AS SOON AS HE HAS
MORE DETAILS.
PICKERING

Mr. Secretary: It is with real grief that I have the honor of acknowledging the reception of your communication of the 15th, announcing the horrid crime that has deprived the United States of its Chief Magistrate.

The sentiments of respect and affection which I personally entertain for the honorable Secretary of State and Mr. Frederick Seward, induce me to hope their injuries will have no serious consequences.

A. BERGHMANS.
Hon. William Hunter, Acting Secretary of State.

title: UN SECRETARY GENERAL ELECTIONS
body:
QUAI UN DIRECTOR ST. LEGIER TOLD EMBOFF DECEMBER 6
THAT UNSYG WALDHEIM WOULD HAVE MORE THAN THE NINE
REQUISITE YES VOTES FOR RE-ELECTION, INCLUDING FRANCE,
UK, US, USSR, ITALY, JAPAN, AND SWEDEN PLUS AFRICANS.
HENCE ONLY QUESTION IS WHETHER CHINESE WILL VETO.
FRANCE'S INFORMATION THAT CHINA WOULD NOT STAND IN WAY
OF WALDHEIM ELECTION CAME FROM FORMER FOREIGN MINISTER
CHIAO AND THEREFORE IS NO LONGER NECESSARILY VALID;
BUT ALL FRENCH ATTEMPTS TO GET NEW READING ON THIS
MATTER FROM PEKING  PROVOKED ONLY WILD GIGGLES,
ACCORDING ST. LEGIER.  HE EMPHASIZED THAT AFRICAN
GROUP SUPPORT FOR WALDHEIM REMAINS SOLID AND AT LEAST
FIVE AFRICAN GOVERNMENTS HAVE MADE DEMARCHES TO PEKING
PLEADING THAT CHINA NOT OPPOSE SYG'S RE-ELECTION.
RUSH

title: SAHSA AIRPLANE CRASH
body:
1. AMBASSADOR SANCHEZ WAS RELEASED FROM HOSPITAL TODAY AFTER OVERNIGHT
OBSERVATION. ALSO RELEASED WERE WILLIS, MEIZLER, SOLEM AND BROWNLOW.
NO US CITIZEN REMAINS HOSPITALIZED.
2. ALTHOUGH MINIFEST LISTS SEVERAL OTHER US CITIZENS AS PASSENGERS
APPARENTLY NONE REQUIRED MEDICAL TREATMENT AND EMBASSY HAS NOT BEEN
ABLE TO LOCATE THEM THROUGH HOSPITALS OR HOTELS.
3. APPARENTLY ALL INJURIES RECEIVED WERE RESULT OF EVACUATION OF
AIRPLANE RATHER THAN CRASH LANDING ITSELF. MOST SERIOUS INJURY REPORTED
WAS BROKEN ANKLE, OTHERS SUFFERED SPRAINS AND ABRASIONS FROM LEAVING
AIRCRAFT.
4. ACCORDING TO SAHSA DAMAGE TO AIRCRAFT WILL REQUIRE AT LEAST 6-8
WEEKS REPAIR.
SANCHEZ

title: Admiral Winslow to the Secretary of the Navy.
body:
[Telegrams.]

 
M-3240. Indians again raiding Yaqui Valley, attacking settlers at Ontagota and the experimental station at San Pedro. Reported that troops and people were deserting Ontagota and that General Obregon has ordered six hundred cavalry from Esperanza who should arrive at Ontagota between 8 and 12 tonight. One thousand troops have left Magdalena enroute to Yaqui Valley via Guaymas and it is hoped that they will arrive in the valley tomorrow. I do not understand that Americans are leaving the valley. Am I to land troops if General is willing? Immediate answer requested.


Winslow.

title: MAJOR OIL SPILL ACCORDING TO NEWSPAPER \"ESTADO DE SAO PAULO\", LARGE  OIL SPILL OCCURRED JAN 9 AT PORT OF SAO SEBASTIAO, MAJOR PETROBRAS TE
body:
ACCORDING TO NEWSPAPER "ESTADO DE SAO PAULO", LARGE OIL SPILL OCCURRED
JAN 9 AT PORT OF SAO SEBASTIAO, MAJOR PETROBRAS TERMINAL ON NORTHERN
COAST OF STATE OF SAO PAULO IN CHANNEL BETWEEN ISLAND "ILHABELA" AND
MAINLAND. OIL TANKER "BRAZILIAN MARINA" (350 METERS LENGTH, 60 METERS
WIDTH, LOADED DRAFT OF 23 METERS, 320 THOUSAND TON CAPACITY IN 15
TANKS, LIBERIAN REGISTRY UNDER PETROBRAS CHARTER) ALLEGEDLY STRUCK
ROCK IN CHANNEL WHILE UNDER TOW, TWO OF TANKS WERE RUPTURED AND
RELEASED 40 THOUSAND TONS OF OIL WHICH HINDERED RESCUE OPERATIONS.
ECOLOGICAL EFFECTS NOT YET ASCERTAINED BUT EXPECTED ALONG ALL BEACHES
OF NORTHERN SAO PAULO STATE. PORT CAPTAIN REPORTEDLY STATED THAT SUCH
OCCURRENCES WERE FREQUENT IN POST OF SUCH ACTIVITY AS SAO SEBASTIAO
AND THAT SUBMARINE CABLES LINKING ILHABELA TO SHORE HAD TWICE
PREVIOUSLY BEEN BROKEN BY LARGE TANKERS.
JOHNSON

title: SUSPENSION OF U.S. OIL IMPORT FEES AND DUTIES
body:
1.  THE PRESIDENT ANNOUNCED IN HIS ENERGY SPEECH APRIL 5
THAT HE PROPOSED TO SUSPEND TEMPORARILY EXISTING
LICENSE FEES AND DUTIES APPLICABLE TO IMPORTED CRUDE OIL
AND PETROLEUM PRODUCTS, IN ORDER TO EASE SHORT-RUN
INFLATIONARY PRESSURES.  (FULL TEXT OF SPEECH WAS
CARRIED ON USICA WIRELESS FILE.)  SUSPENSION WAS ORDERED
IN PRESIDENTIAL PROCLAMATION 4655 ON APRIL 6 (PUBLISHED
IN FEDERAL REGISTER APRIL 9), WHICH LIFTED THE FEES FOR
THE PERIOD APRIL 1 THROUGH JUNE 30, 1979.  PROCLAMATION
PROVIDES THAT THE SECRETARY OF ENERGY MAY DEFER
REIMPOSITION OF THE LICENSE FEES AND IMPORT DUTY ON ANY
TYPE OF CRUDE OIL, UNFINISHED OIL OR FINISHED PRODUCT FOR
NOT MORE THAN TWO ADDITIONAL PERIODS, EACH OF SIX MONTHS'
DURATION, IF THE SECRETARY FINDS THAT IMPOSITION OF THE
FEES WOULD NOT BE IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PURPOSES OF THE
PROCLAMATION.  CHRISTOPHER

title: The Mexican Ambassador to the Secretary of State.
body:
[Memorandum.]

The Government of Mexico has received reliable information to the effect that yesterday the Federal authorities at San Antonio, Tex., found 100 carbines of 45 caliber, with 5,000 cartridges for the same, in the possession of an American friend of Madero. My Government has also learned that the said authorities had already requested instructions to seize these arms. The American maintains that he bought them for legitimate commerce.
The Mexican ambassador hastens very respectfully to communicate these reports to the Department of State so that the case may be investigated, the responsibility fixed where it belongs, and steps be taken to prevent the commission of acts that may be prejudicial to the maintenance of peace in Mexico.

ANNOUNCED THAT HE SATISFIED PEACE, LAW AND ORDER NOW PREVAIL

body:
EMBASSY IS REPEATING FOLLOWING MESSAGE SENT BY AMCONGEN
GUADALAJARA.  QUOTE SIX BOMB EXPLOSIONS SHOOK GUADALAJARA
IN THE EARLY MORNING HOURS OF JANUARY 9.  BANKS, A TRAVEL
AGENCY, A FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OFFICE AND THE CTM (CONFED-
ERACION DE TRABAJADORES DE MEXICO) HEADQUARTERS BUILDING
WERE HIT BUT NO EXTENSIVE DAMAGE HAS BEEN REPORTED.
PRELIMINARY REPORTS ATTRIBUTE THE BOMBINGS TO TERRORISTS
ELEMENTS BUT NO CONFIRMATION OF THIS HAS YET BEEN OBTAINED.
POLICE AND THE MILITARY HAVE BEEN MOBILIZED TO PATROL
STRATEGIC PARTS OF THE CITY.  THE BOMBINGS WERE THE FIRST
TO OCCUR IN GUADALAJARA SINCE LAST SEPTEMBER 'S EXPLOSIONS
WHICH COINCIDED WITH BOMBINGS IN MEXICO CITY AND OAXACA.
NO INCIDENTS HAVE OCCURRED AT THE CONSULATE BUT GUARDS
HAVE BEEN ALERTED TO TAKE SPECIAL PRECAUTIONS.  MORE DE-
TAILED INFORMATION WILL BE FORWARDED AS SOON AS OBTAINED.
END QUOTE.  LUCEY

title: The Consul General at Dairen (Benninghoff) to the Secretary of State

61. Information re Sino-Soviet negotiations still not available here. However, Chinese press reports as contained in Mukden's 75, April 19 and previous to Nanking confirm this office's former belief that Soviets would endeavor impose conditions re takeover which Chinese would find difficult to accept.
Meanwhile preparations for takeover continue. Present local regime reported burning or removing documents Port Arthur. Political prisoners apparently being released. Cooperatives and other official enterprises Dairen dominated by Communists closing. Movement of Communists to Korea or elsewhere continues although reliable reports received by organized underground left in Dairen. Soviets  reliably reported told Sino-Communists refrain from violence after takeover (disturbances here would cut down commercial value to Soviets of open port), also over 50 families Japanese technicians [and] specialists transferred Harbin via Korea.

CAMEROON NOT QUALIFIED FOR TITLE III AND THAT THIS PROGRAM
SHOULD BE INITIATED IN OTHER AFRICAN COUNTRIES WHERE LOW FOOD
PRODUCTION IS MAJOR PROBLEM.

body:
1. HONG KONG PRC-OWNED WEN WEI PAO MARCH 7 CARRIES ARTICLE
ON PRESENCE OF "USS OKINAWA" IN GULF OF SIAM. ARTICLE
SUGGESTS A PARALLEL BETWEEN THE OKINAWA'S CURRENT MISSION
AND 1965 LANDING OF MARINES FORM THE "BOXER" IN DOMINICAN
REPUBLIC "TO PROTECT US CITIZENS," LEAVING OPEN TO QUESTION

PRESIDENT FORD'S EFFORTS TO OBTAIN INCREASED MILITARY AID FOR
CAMBODIA FROM CONGRESS. REVIEW ALSO INCLUDES ASSISTANT
SECRETARY HIBIB'S STATEMENT THAT US HAD SOUGHT "PEACE TALKS"
FOR FIVE MONTHS, WITHOUT OBTAINING ANY "POSITIVE REACTION."
SPECULATING, THE COLUMNIST LINKS THE BABIB STATEMENT ON
TALKS WITH THE PRESIDENT'S REQUEST BUT WONDERS WHAT
ASSISTANT SECRETARY'S "ULTERIOR MOTIVE" MAY BE.
CROSS

title: Municipal Council of Birmingham
body:
Borough of Birmingham.
At a quarterly meeting of the council of this borough, held in the council chamber at the public office, Moor street, on the 4th day of May, 1865, Henry Wiggen, esq., mayor, in the chair, it was moved by the mayor, seconded by Mr. Alderman Holliday, and

Resolved unanimously, That this council desires to express to the government of the United States its abhorrence and detestation of the atrocious crime which has deprived the American nation of its chief; that while manifesting its horror at the foul deed which sacrificed the life of the President, at the moment when victory had crowned his efforts with success, this council desires to record its deep and earnest sympathy with the government and people of the United States on this great calamity.
[seal.] HENRY WIGGEN, 
Mayor.

body:

TARGETED FOR PANAMA, EXCEPT FOR TRAINING UNDER FMS
CONTRACTS ENTERED INTO PRIOR TO FY 1975.

MILITARY ATTACHE TO EXAMINE ITEM BY ITEM ALL OTHER
OUTSTANDING ORDERS.   BROWN

title: CENTRAL BANK REQUEST FOR IMF ASSISTANCE
body:
1.  DURING JULY 19 MEETING CENTRAL BANK GOVERNOR SAMBWA TOLD ME THAT
HE PLANS TO ASK THE IMF TO PROVIDE TWO EXPERTS TO WORK IN THE BANK.
HE SAID THAT IT WAS OF COURSE IMPORTANT THAT THEY BE FRENCH-SPEAKING
AND THAT HE WAS THEREFORE ASKING FOR ONE OF THE EXPERTS TO COME FROM
A FRANCOPHONE COUNTRY.  HOWEVER, HE SAID HE WOULD LIKE THE SECOND
EXPERT TO BE AN AMERICAN, RECALLING THE EXCELLENT EXPERIENCE HE HAD
HAD WITH AN AMERICAN IMF REPRESENTATIVE WHO WORKED FOR THE BANK
UNTIL ABOUT TWO YEARS AGO.  HE ASKED IF WE COULD ASSIST IN LOCATING
A GOOD MAN FOR THE JOB.
2.  IN VIEW OF THE GOZ'S INTEREST AND OBVIOUS NEED, I RECOMMEND THAT
THE DEPARTMENT CONTACT THE IMF WITH A VIEW TO ASSURING A POSITIVE
RESPONSE TO SAMBWA'S REQUEST.
CUTLER

title: RUMOR OF GREEK INTEREST IN F-16 AIRCRAFT
body:
1.  WE HAVE HEARD FROM A NON-TURKISH SOURCE THAT THE GREEKS
INTEND TO PURCHASE FORTY F-16 AIRCRAFT AND THAT THE GOG HAS
INITIATED CONTACTS WITH GENERAL DYNAMICS IN THIS RESPECT.
IF THIS REPORT IS ACCURATE, WE WISH TO POINT OUT THAT THE
TURKS WILL ALMOST CERTAINLY FEEL THEY MUST HAVE F-16 OR SIMILAR
AIRCRAFT, JUST AS THEY DID IN THE EARLY 1970 WHEN THE GREEKS
MOVED TO ACQUIRE F-4. WHILE UNDER CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES THE
F-16 IS A POSSIBLE NEXT GENERATION OF FIGHTER AIRCRAFT FOR
NATO FORCES, INCLUDING PERHAPS BOTH GREECE AND TURKEY IN THE
MID-1980 AND BEYOND, COMPETITION BETWEEN THE TWO NATIONS
AT THIS TIME OVER ACQUIRING THE F-16 WOULD NOT, WE WOULD
VENTURE, SERVE U.S. INTERESTS IN THIS AREA.
2.  ACTION REQUESTED:  WE WOULD APPRECIATE RECEIVING ANY
INFORMATION AVAILABLE TO THE DEPARTMENT OR IN ATHENS REGARDING
THE RUMORED GREEK PURCHASE OF F-16.
SPIERS

[Telegram.]

 
My April 1. Peruvian counter proposal on the basis of dividing territories, received yesterday by Chilean Minister for Foreign Affairs through Brazilian Minister, was found utterly unacceptable as Chile needs both territories for military defense. The Minister for Foreign Affairs says he told Brazil that Chile would be disposed to pay as much as three million pounds sterling indemnity for both Tacna and Arica and that if Peru would accept the decision of a third nation or of the United States, Brazil and Argentina on the basis that Chile will keep Tacna and Arica, Chile would be willing to pay even more should the Powers so decide, and also to cede Tarata.


Pierrepont.

title: The Ambassador in Mexico (Messersmith) to the Secretary of State
body:
A-2709. Reference MacLean's conversation on September 13 with O'Donoghue re increasing total of Mexican workers being repatriated if they were transported by vessel to Tampico.
After discussion of question with competent authorities, Embassy is able to state that Mexican National lines can not handle any number of repatriates in excess of 20,900 monthly. Even though these workers were transported to Tampico or other ports by vessel, they would still have to be brought to interior of Republic and strain on National lines would be same as though they were brought to Mexico via Laredo or El Paso. In other words, equipment and rolling stock directed to Tampico or other ports for purpose indicated would have to be taken from Laredo or El Paso runs with consequent reduction in equipment available for the return of Mexican workers from those ports of entry.


Messersmith

Sir: I have the honor to inform you that the Madrid papers of yesterday, upon the authority of the minister of the treasury, announce the signing of a commercial treaty between Spain and Switzerland on Saturday, September 1, subject to approval by the Cortes. It is also announced that, beginning on September 5, a modus vivendi between the two nations will go into effect, pending consideration of the treaty. As soon as the Gaceta containing the exchange of notes by which the modus vivendi was established reach here copies will be sent you.
I have, etc.
Wm. Miller Collier.

title: The Swiss Minister ( Sulzer ) to the Secretary of State
body:
Sir: I am instructed by my Government to transmit to your Excellency, upon the special request of the German Government, the following protest:
"According to annex 1 to the armistice agreement, Belgium, France, Luxemburg, and Alsace-Lorraine are to be evacuated within 15 days in three stages. The third stage reaches over into Rhenish (Rhineland) territory, on the map, west of Prum and between Merzig and Saargemund, including Saarlouis and Saarbrucken.
It appears possible that this was done in order to attempt to add these regions to Alsace-Lorraine or to Luxemburg. The protest of the members of the German Commission was not heeded. The German Government most solemnly protests against any attempt to tear away these territories.
(Signed) Solf,Secretary of State in the Foreign Office.
Berlin, November 21, 1918."

Accept [etc.]


Hans Sulzer

title: The Ambassador in Chile (Philip) to the Secretary of State
body:
6. Department's 3, January 14, 4 [5] p.m. Two officials of the Chilean Ministry of Foreign Affairs recently have mentioned the receipt of cables from the Chilean Ambassador in Washington to the effect that I had been specifically instructed by the Department to propose a new modus vivendi which shall remain in force until superseded by a commercial treaty between the United States and Chile.
I understand the instruction received leaves me discretion in the matter and I have not yet broached its contents to the Minister for Foreign Affairs as my information now indicates that the French Parliament will not ratify the Franco-Chilean convention of January 16, 1936 in the near future. In such case our existing agreement of September 28, 1931 should remain in force.
I am carefully watching the situation and will at once inform the Department of any action taken.
Philip

body:
AMBASSADOR-DESIGNATE TO U.S. ANTONIO AZEREDO DA SILVEIRA
IN JUNE 11 STATEMENT IN RIO DE JANEIRO JUST PRIOR TO HIS
DEPARTURE FOR U.S., IS QUOTED BY PRESS AS REMARKING
THAT HE FORESEES ADOPTION OF NEW FORMS OF COOPERATION
BETWEEN BRAZIL AND U.S. AND IS HONORED AND PLEASED WITH
HIS NEW POSITION. "BRAZIL", HE REPORTEDLY SAID, "IS
TODAY A GREAT COUNTRY WITH A LARGE INTERNATIONAL STANDING.
ON THE OTHER HAND, THE UNITED STATES IS A COUNTRY OF
EXTRAORDINARY POWER, THE ACTIONS OF WHICH HAVE INFLUENCE
THROUGHOUT THE WORLD. I HOPE THAT WE, WHO KNEW HOW TO
COLLABORATE IN TWO WARS, WILL ALWAYS BE UNITED BY THE STRONG
TIES OF FRIENDSHIP THAT HAVE ALWAYS EXISTED BETWEEN US."
SILVEIRA, ACCORDING TO PRESS, ALSO STATED THAT "BRAZIL
EXPECTS, NOW IN THIS TIME OF PEACE, THE SAME COOPERATION
(FROM THE U.S.) WHICH WAS GIVEN BY BRAZIL) TO THE UNITED
STATES DURING THE WAR".
SAYRE

title: The Ambassador in the Soviet Union (Steinhardt) to the Secretary of State

1580. The Moscow newspapers today publish the full text of the note handed by Molotov to the Iranian Ambassador in Moscow on the morning of August 25 announcing that by virtue of article 6 of the Soviet-Iranian Treaty of 1921, Soviet troops were temporarily entering the territory of Iran for the purpose of self-defense. It is presumed that the full text of this lengthy note has been published in the American newspapers or has otherwise been brought to the Department's attention.
A brief Tass despatch from Tiflis is also published stating that on the morning of August 25 Soviet troops crossed the frontier and advanced 40 miles toward Ardebil and Tabriz and that the advance was continuing. No reference was made in the despatch to opposition by Iranian forces.


Steinhardt

My dear Mr. Secretary: Some time ago [March 9] I had the honor to present to your excellency a note setting forth the reasons which, in my opinion, should operate to induce the Government of the United States to interpose its good offices before the Government of Panama for the purpose of bringing about the acceptance by that Government of the award of the Chief Justice in the Costa Rica-Panama Boundary Arbitration.

This [etc.]

body:
ARY
1. DEPARTMENT HAS RECEIVED COPY OF MAY 20 LETTER TO AMBAS-
SADOR SNEIDER FROM JOHN B. WALKER, AMERICAN MISSIONARY
RESIDENT IN JAPAN, WHO CLAIMS THAT HE WAS DETAINED
BY KOREAN OFFICIALS AT KIMPO AIRPORT FOR SIX HOURS MAY 19
ON RETURN FROM VISIT TO SEOUL.  WALKER WROTE THAT KOREAN
OFFICIALS TOLD HIM THAT HE HAD VIOLATED IMMIGRATION LAW,
LAW AGAINST TRANSPORTING ANTI-KOREAN DOCUMENTS AND EM-9,
AND THAT OFFICIALS CONFISCATED DOCUMENTS FROM HIS PERSON AND
LUGGAGE.

WALKER, WHEN SENT, TO FACILITATE REPLIES TO INTERESTED
AMERICANS WHO HAVE INQUIRED ABOUT INCIDENT.
3.  WALKER ALSO WROTE KOREAN AMBASSADOR TO JAPAN DEMANDING
RETURN OF DOCUMENTS AND A SERIES OF APOLOGIES.
4.  COPIES OF BOTH LETTERS POUCHED.  VANCE

title: NEWSWEEK INTERVIEW WITH THE SECRETARY SCOTT SULLIVAN HAS WRITTEN TO  REMIND YOU OF HIS REQUEST TO INTERVIEW THE SECRETARY AS PART OF AN EXTENSIVE
body:
SCOTT SULLIVAN HAS WRITTEN TO REMIND YOU OF HIS REQUEST
TO INTERVIEW THE SECRETARY AS PART OF AN EXTENSIVE
PRESENTATION ON PRESIDENT FORD PLANNED BY NEWSWEEK.
SULLIVAN WOULD LIKE TO SPEAK WITH THE SECRETARY ON THE
RECORD FOR A FEW MINUTES "FOR HIS IMPRESSIONS OF FORD
AS A FOREIGN POLICY FIGURE", FOLLOWED BY A BACKGROUNDER
(IN HIS WORDS) "TO GET SOME FEEL OF HOW THE SECRETARY
AND THE PRESIDENT WORK TOGETHER, STRENGTHS AND WEAKNESSES,
THE FEEL OF MAJOR CRISES LIKE MAYAGUEZ AND ANYTHING ELSE
THE SECRETARY MIGHT BE WILLING TO OFFER."
SCOTT'S DEADLINE IS SEPTEMBER 24, BUT HE COULD UPDATE
ON THE 27TH OR 28TH.
SULLIVAN SAID THAT YOU SUGGESTED WE REMIND YOU OF THE PROP
SITION,  WHICH HE SAYS HE HAS ALREADY DISCUSSED WITH YOU.
IF THE SECRETARY AGREES TO SUCH AN INTERVIEW, S/PRS WILL
MAKE THE NECESSARY ARRANGEMENTS UPON NOTIFICATION.
ROBINSON

title: KNESSET RESOLUTION
body:
THE FOLLOWING IS THE EMBASSY'S TRANSLATION OF THE OFFICIAL
TEXT OF THE RESOLUTION ADOPTED BY THE KNESSET ON DECEMBER
19:
1.  THE KNESSET DETERMINES THAT THE SUBMITTING OF NEW AND
OBDURATE EGYPTIAN DEMANDS PREVENTED THE SIGNATURE OF THE
PEACE TREATY BETWEEN ISRAEL AND EGYPT.
2.  THE KNESSET DETERMINES THAT THE POSITION OF THE U.S.
ADMINISTRATION, PLACING RESPONSIBILITY FOR NON-SIGNATURE
OF THE PEACE TREATY ON ISRAEL, IS ONE-SIDED AND UNJUST,
AND DOES NOT CONTRIBUTE TO FURTHERING PEACE.
3.  ISRAEL DESIRES PEACE AND HAS MADE MANY SACRIFICES FOR
ITS SAKE.  SHE WILL CONTINUE TO WORK FOR ITS ACHIEVEMENT,
BUT CANNOT ACCEPT PROPOSALS THAT JEOPARDIZE HER SECURITY
AND WELFARE. LEWIS

body:

THAT WESTINGHOUSE ELECTRIC CORPORATION HAS SUED THE U.S.
REGULATORY COMMISSION (NRC) FOR "DELAYING FOR TWO YEARS

title: 89. Memorandum From R.C. Bowman of the National Security Council Staff to the Executive Secretary of the National Security Council (Smith)
body:
I have attached two JCS papers that you might like to scan. I have not heard any more about the command system study since I spoke to you about it in February.

JCSM 129 indicates the Chiefs' general agreement with the study with the exception that they felt it underrates the Alternate Command Center at Fort Ritchie. At that time the Chiefs deferred judgment on the Command Post Afloat.
In the second paper, JCSM 364 (17 May), they concluded that two command ships are essential, and that the capabilities of the USS Northampton should be improved. The Chief of Naval Operations disagreed, and argued that one ship was sufficient.
In the last analysis, the value of any command facility must be determined to a great extent by the probability that the President will, in fact, make use of that facility.



RCB

title: Mr. Seward to Mr. Haldeman.
body:
No. 28.]

Sir: Your interesting despatch of the 24th of last month (No. 28) has been received. The President is gratified to learn that you found, on your recent return to Stockholm, after an absence of several months, the same friendly feeling and sympathy existing on the part of his Majesty's government towards the United States that have been constantly manifested throughout the period of our painful and protracted struggle for the maintenance of the national authority. The sentiments of Count Manderstrom, as expressed in your interview with him, are such as might have been expected from a statesman of his well known clear perceptions and solid judgment.
I am, sir, your obedient servant,

WILLIAM H. SEWARD.
Jacob S. Haldeman, Esq., &c., &c., &c., Stockholm.

Secretary Dulles held a press conference on July 28. In response to a reporter's question about the growing strength of the Tudeh Party in Iran, the Secretary replied as follows: 
"Recent developments in Iran, especially the growing activity of the illegal Communist party, which appears to be tolerated by the Iranian Government have caused us concern. These developments make it more difficult for the United States to give assistance to Iran so long as its government tolerates this sort of activity."
The text of the Secretary's statement is printed in Department of State Bulletin, August 10, 1953, page 178.

title: RAINS ARRIVE
body:
THE RAINS HAVE COME IN ABUNDANCE THROUGHOUT TUNISIA,
ENDING TWO MONTHS' DROUGHT.  ALTHOUGH BOTH PRIME
MINISTER AND MINISTER AGRICULTURE IN TALKS WITH
EMBASSY LAST WEEK SEEMED CONFIDENT REGARDING AGRICULTURE
SITUATION, OTHER OFFICIALS, AGRICULTURAL EXPERTS AND
GENERAL PUBLIC WERE EXPRESSING INCREASING CONCERN.
TIJANI CHELLI, PDG INVESTMENT PROMOTION AGENCY, IN
PARTICULAR NOTED THAT IF RAINS DID NOT FALL SOON HIS
HOPES FOR INDUSTRIAL INVESTMENT WOULD RECEIVE SETBACK
SINCE SUBSTANTIAL FOREX WOULD HAVE TO BE DIVERTED TO
FOOD IMPORTS.  IN ANY CASE, IT IS BELIEVED THAT UNLESS
RAINS FOR REST OF SEASON ARE UNUSUALLY HEAVY, CEREALS
PRODUCTION WILL PROBABLY BE 20-30 PERCENT BELOW EARLY
ESTIMATE OF 1.1 MILLION TONS.  FOR EXAMPLE, RAINS HAVE
COME TOO LATE IN SOUTH TO SAVE MORE THAN 50 PERCENT
OF BARLEY CROP BUT WILL BE EXCELLENT FOR PASTURAGE
AND REPLENISHMENT OF GROUND WATER.
SEELYE

body:
407. Your 531, September 1, 3 p.m.
For Walter L. Brown.
This Government is in full sympathy with all practicable efforts for Russian relief, but believes that at this time American relief should be administered through the private agency of the American Relief Administration. It is thought that full information will be obtained in this way without the risk of complications through governmental action. This Government therefore will not for the present take part in the proceedings of the International Commission. It is understood that all actual relief can be coordinated on the spot with that afforded by the American Relief Administration.
Keep Department fully advised of all proceedings of International Commission.
Hughes

Henry F. Grady

TEST OF OPINION COULD BEST BE CONDUCTED.

title: 349. National Security Action Memorandum No. 251
body:
TO
The Secretary of State
 Before approving the proposed aide-memoire on U.S. aid to Greece arising out of the Papaligouras visit, the President would like the Department's estimate of the Greek political outlook. In particular he wonders what sort of alternative cabinets could emerge from the current political crisis, and what the likely implications for U.S. interests of each might be. If we face the prospect of prolonged jockeying and possible renewed instability in Greek politics, is there anything the U.S. could or should do about it?
McGeorge Bundy

title: POSSIBLE TRANSFER OF SWISS MILITARY ATTACHE FROM WARSAW TO EAST BERLIN
body:
1. EMBOFF LEARNED FROM A SWISS EMBASSY CONTACT( BODENMUELLER)
THAT THE SWISS ARE CONSIDERING TRANSFERRING THEIR MILITARY
ATTACHED FROM WARSAW TO BERLIN IN THE NEAR FUTURE. THE
PRESENT ATTACHE, COLONEL VITTORINO RANZONI, RESIDES IN
WARSAW AND IS ACCREDITED TO POLAND, CZECHOSLOVAKIA AND THE
GDR. ACCORDING TO BODENMUELLER, THE MOVE WOULD SIMPLIFY
COL. RANZONI'S OFFICIAL FUNCTIONS, NOT THE LEAST BECAUSE
LANGUAGE BARRIERS WOULD BE REMOVED. HE ALSO HINTED THAT
RESIDENCE IN EAST BERLIN WOULDFACILITATE THE ATTACHE'S
UNOFFICIAL ACCESS TO CONTACTS IN WEST BERLIN, WHICH HE
DESCRIBED AS PROBABLY WELL-INFORMED ON WARSAW PACT
MATTERS.
2. BODENMUELER EMPHASIZED THAT THE MOVE WOULD BE
SIMPLY A CHANGE OF RESIDENCE WITHOUT ANY POLITICAL
IMPLICATIONS. THERE WOULD BE NO CHANGE IN THE ATTACHE'S
CURRENT ACCREDITATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES.COOPER

title: The Minister in Nicaragua (Nicholson) to the Secretary of State
body:
86. Department's telegram No. 69, September 25, 7 p.m. The Minister for Foreign Affairs says that Nicaragua's attitude toward the Honduran protest is still undecided as he has not yet consulted the President. He feels that the Honduran Government is endeavoring to exploit the incident with a view to impairing indirectly the authority and work of the Mediation Commission and will insist that any proposal for settlement of the present misunderstanding embody a clause providing that the Commission's endeavors shall in no way be affected. He feels personally that Nicaragua should not put forward the offer of settlement; that if Honduras fails to do so, the proposal of a third party, preferably the United States, would receive friendly consideration.
He says that President Somoza may desire that Nicaragua take the initiative in making this offer.
Nicholson

title: CHABBAL NAMED CNRS HEAD
body:
1.  COUNCIL OF MINISTERS ANNOUNCED AUGUST 4 APPOINTMENT
OF ROBERT CHABBAL, DIRECTOR GENERAL OF THE CENTRE
NATIONAL DE LA RECHERCHE SCIENTIFIQUE (CNRS).  THIS
APPOINTMENT CONCLUDES A SERIES OF CHANGES AT THE HEAD
OF FRANCE'S LARGEST RESEARCH ORGANIZATIONS.  ON JUNE
30 HUBERT CURIEN, PREVIOUSLY HEAD OF THE DELEGATION
GENERALE A LA RECHERCHE SCIENTIFIQUE ET TECHNIQUE
(DGRST), REPLACED MAURICE LEVY AS HEAD OF THE CENTRE
NATIONAL D'ETUDES SPATIALES (CNES).  ON JULY 7 PREVIOUS
CNRS DIRECTOR BERNARD GREGORY WAS NAMED HEAD OF DGRST.
2.  CHABBAL, BORN IN 1927 AND A PHYSICS PH.D., HAS BEEN
ASSOCIATED WITH THE UPPER LEVELS OF THE FRENCH
SCIENTIFIC ESTABLISHMENT FOR A QUARTER OF A CENTURY.
AMONG HIS MORE IMPORTANT POSTS HAVE BEEN DIRECTOR OF
THE AIME-COTON LABORATORY (1962-69), SCIENTIFIC
DIRECTOR OF CNRS FOR PHYSICS, AND SCIENTIFIC COUNSELOR
TO THE SECRETAIRE D'ETAT AUX UNIVERSITES MME. ALICE
SAUNIER-SEITE.

ADVISORY COMMITTEE AND OTHERS TO PROCEED ALONG THESE LINES.
KISSINGER

title: Consul Letcher to the Secretary of State
body:
[Telegram]

 
Referring to removal Colonel Brown to Adela to facilitate the receipt of supplies, I submit that heretofore I have been very successful in employing my good offices with local authorities in securing shipment supplies to our troops at San Antonio, but in view of the circumstances which have lately arisen and the evident purpose of the superior Mexican authorities to force withdrawal of American troops by creating difficulties as much as possible, I do not feel quite sure that further shipments may be made over railroad for military use. I have reason to believe, also, that prohibition of use of telegraph and landing in towns or even passing over by aeroplanes is under consideration. Circumstances seem to indicate that Carranza troops are concentrated around the command of Colonel Brown pending settlement of demands for withdrawal of troops.


Letcher

title: TURKISH ATTITUDE ON THE SVALBARD (SPITZBERGEN)
body:
1.GOT HAS ISSUED NO STATEMENT ON SVALBARD WITHIN PAST
TWO YEARS. ACCORDING TO MFA WORKING-LEVEL SPECIALIST ON
LAW OF THE SEA, MFA'S PERCEPTION OF THE DISPUTE IS THAT
NORWAY ARGUES THAT A MEDIAN LINE SHOULD BE APPLIED IN THE
BARENTS SEA; THE USSR ON OTHER HAND HAD NOT MADE ITS
POSITION CLEAR BUT APPEARED TO ARGUE THAT A SOLUTION SHOULD
BE BASED ON THE "SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES" PERTAINING IN
THE AREA. GOT HAS NO INTENTION OF MAKING ANY COMMENT
ON THE SUBJECT. HOWEVER, THE LOS SPECIALIST WAS
INTERESTED IN THE OUTCOME OF THE TALKS, AND IN PARTICULAR
THE SOVIET ARGUMENTATION FOR "SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCES".
GOT INTEREST WILL FOCUS ON HOW PROGRESS OF TALKS MIGHT
AFFECT TURKEY'S AEGEAN CONTINENTAL
SHELF DISPUTE WITH GREECE, HE SAID.
MACOMBER

THE SECRETARY-GENERAL




                                                         17 December 2007



        Dear Mr. Kassow,

                I have the honour to inform you that at its 62nd plenary meeting in
        November 2007, the General Assembly decided to confirm your appointment
        as a regular member of the United Nations Investments Committee for a
        three-year term of office commencing on 1 January 2008 and expiring on
        31 December 2010. I greatly appreciate your willingness to serve on the
        Committee and,as an acknowledgement of your valuable participation,
        decided to seek the confirmation of the General Assembly to appoint you as a
        regular member.

               In extending my congratulations to you on the confirmation of your
        appointment, I wish to take this opportunity to wish you a very happy and
        successful 2008.

                                                          Yours sincerely,




                                                            Ban Ki-




         Mr. Achim Kassow
         Member of the Board of Managing Directors
         Commerzbank AG

[Telegram.]

Mr. Mizner informs Mr. Blaine that he has arranged for telegrams five times monthly each way through La Libertad by steamer to and from San Jose with the assurance that they may be sent from La Libertad direct by way of Honduras, if possible. title: BC GAS SUPPLIES TO US CUT
body:
1.  POWER FAILURES AND MECHANICAL BREAKDOWNS CAUSED BY
EXTREME WEATHER CONDITIONS HAVE RESULTED IN MASSIVE SHORTFALL
OF BC GAS DELIVERIES TO US CONSUMERS IN WASHINGTON STATE.
SHORTFALL REACHED 400 MCF BELOW CONTRACTED DEMAND JANUARY 9
AND HAS BEEN WELL OVER 200 MCF  FOR PAST WEEK.  BREAK IN
WEATHER WILL OFFER SOME RELIEF BUT SERIOUS SHORTFALLS
EXPECTED TO CONTINUE FOR ANOTHER WEEK AT LEAST.
2.  WIND CHILL FACTOR OF 95 BELOW ZERO FROZE TOTAL OF 14
WELLS THIS PAST WEEK.  WELLS WERE OPERATING AT PEAK
CAPACITY BRINGING UP GROUND WATER CAUSING FREEZUPS.  BRIEF
POWERFAILURE EARLIER IN WEEK SHUT DOWN GAS PROCESSING
PLANT. EMERGENCY CREWS REPAIRING DAMAGE AND BREAK IN
WEATHER WILL FACILITIATE REPAIRS BUT SITUATION NOT EXPECTED
TO EASE FOR SEVERAL DAYS.
3.  PRODUCERS CLAIM GAS BEING PUMPED TOO RAPIDLY FROM
EXISTING WELLS BUT THAT NEW WELLS UNECONOMICAL UNDER TERMS
OF FEDERAL RESOURCE TAXATION MEASURES.
STUTESMAN

title: Documentos utilizados como subsídios nas conversações entre o ministro das Relações Exteriores do Brasil, Azeredo da Silveira, e o secretário de Estado norte-americano, Henry Kissenger. São notas, resumos, relatórios, discursos e correspondência, tratando de diversos assuntos, no âmbito das relações entre os dois países e da política internacional, com ênfase nas questões econômicas e comerciais, tais como no intercâmbio comercial de diversos produtos, taxação de tarifas para exportação e importação, protecionismo e relações financeiras. Inclui informações sobre a situação política interna de diversos países, principalmente América Latina e sobre reforma da Organização dos Estados Americanos (OEA). Há ainda documentação sobre a relação dos Estados Unidos com China e URSS, sobre candidatura a cargos da ONU e da OEA, sobre reuniões da Comissão dos Direitos Humanos, dos chanceleres da Bacia do Prata, do "Policy Planning" e do SELA, sobre direito do mar, a questão da energia nuclear e a situação política do Oriente Médio.

title: Irving S. Friedman Chron files - Correspondence 11
body:
Mr. Andrew M. Kamarck December 19, 1969
Irving 8. Friedman
Proposed Study on the Implications of the United Kingdom
Jeining the Common Market
Mr. Caram requested today that we extend our meat study to include
the possible implications of the United Kingdom joining the Common
Market for meat exports. I suggested that he not make this request as
it would delay the completion of the study by a considerable period of
time, perhaps months. However, I said this raised a question of
considerable importance for various commodities in a number of developing
countries, and I would consider doing such a paper to include a section
on meat.
I do think it would be worthwhile to prepare a paper on possible
implications of the United Kingdom joining the Common Market for principal
commodities of the countries most affected.
Your reaction would be appreciated.
ce: Mr. Macone

title: SHRIMPING ACTIVITY HALTED IN TAMPICO ON FEBRUARY 13 BOAT OWNERS IN  TAMPICO KEPT THEIR 200 SHRIMP VESSELS FROM SAILING. REASON GIVEN FOR ACT
body:
ON FEBRUARY 13 BOAT OWNERS IN TAMPICO KEPT THEIR 200
SHRIMP VESSELS FROM SAILING.  REASON GIVEN FOR ACTION WAS
LACK OF CLEAR CUT AGREEMENT WITH COOPERATIVE FISHERMEN.
PRESIDENT OF FISHERMENS COOP FEDERATION STATE TAMAULIPAS
NOTED REASON FOR SHRIMP VESSEL OWNERS ACTION WAS THEIR
INTENT TO INFLUENCE GOM DEP FISHERIES TO DECLARE TAMPICO
UNRESTRICTED FISHING PORT.  THIS WOULD MEAN OWNERS WOULD
NOT HAVE TO HIRE CREW THROUGH CONTRACTUAL ARRANGEMENTS
WITH FISHERMEN COOPERATIVES.  OUTCOME OF SITUATION BEING
CLOSELY WATCHED OWING TO POSSIBLE RENEWED CONFRONTATION
BETWEEN OWNERS AND COOP FISHERMEN ON ISSUE OF TERMS OF
CONTRACT BETWEEN THEM.  DRAFTER ROLF JUHL.  LUCEY

STRATEGIC SERVICES (PROV.), 2677TH REGIMENT, APO 512. HE
AND SEVERALOTHERS, ACCORDING TO ACCOUNTS HERE, WERE LANDED

title: FRG FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO PORTUGAL
body:
ECON/COMMERCIAL MINISTER DISCUSSED POSSIBILITY OF FRG
FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO PORTUGAL ON DECEMBER 22 WITH
CHANCELLOR'S ECONOMIC ADVISOR DR. HISS.  HISS MADE IT
CLEAR THAT FRG WOULD PREFER TO SEE A MULTILATERAL
PACKAGE ARRANGED BY BIS.  WHEN ECON/COMMERCIAL
MINISTER CITED CHANCELLOR SCHMIDT'S DECEMBER 17
TELEVISION STATEMENT, AS REPORTED BY FBIS LONDON
DECEMBER 18, HISS SHOWED CONSIDERABLE RELUCTANCE TO
ADMIT POSSIBILITY OF BILATERAL ASSISTANCE.  HE DID
NOT,HOWEVER COMPLETELY REJECT POSSIBILITY OF SUCH
BILATERAL AID.  FONOFF OFFICIAL RESPONSIBLE FOR
ECONOMIC RELATIONS WITH PORTUGAL TOOK ESSENTIALLY
THE SAME POSITION, BUT TOLD EMBOFF THAT CHANCELLOR'S
REMARKS WERE, AT THE TIME, MORE IN THE NATURE OF
OFF-HAND COMMENTS.  HE CONFESSED THAT THERE WERE
NO SPECIFIC PROPOSALS CURRENTLY UNDER
CONSIDERATION IN  THE FOREIGN OFFICE.  EMBOFF
ALSO LEARNED THAT THE FINANCE MINISTRY HAD NOT TAKEN
THE MATTER UNDER CONSIDERATION.
HILLENBRAND

title: TALK WITH PRIME MINISTER RIFAI--SYRIA AND JORDAN, MANDATE RENEWAL
body:
MANDATE RENEWAL
1. DISCUSSED BRIEFLY WITH RIFAI MAY 12 SYRIAN-JORDANIAN
TALKS IN DAMASCUS LAST WEEKEND. HE CLAIMS TALKS MADE
STEADY PROGRESS, BUT THAT NOTHING SENSATIONAL HAD BEEN
WORKED OUT. FOCUS WAS ON ECONOMIC ISSUES, HE CLAIMS.
HE INDICATED THAT WORLD SHOULD EXPECT NO INSTANT
FEDERATION FROM JORDAN AND SYRIA. HE ADDED THAT "WE DON'T
HAVE INSTANT COFFEE IN MIND. WE PREFER TO PERCOLATE
OUR DRINK."
2. ON UNDOF MANDATE RENEWAL HE TOLD ME ESSENTIALLY

268. Your 198, July 15th, 6 p.m. The two Legations would welcome Department's proposals if possible execution but this unfortunately appears doubtful. Unanimity diplomatic corps on abolition of asylum improbable. Japanese Legation refused to deny asylum 1920. Still harbors Anfus. Right to grant asylum always claimed for French concession Shanghai where Chang Ching-yao recently sheltered. Also opposition certain smaller countries apprehended.
While unanimity diplomatic corps on the proposal for personal responsibility and punitive damages probably obtainable, previous efforts to fix blame through such measures for foreign losses have resulted in failure as in the case of Chang Ching-yao.
Also feared insistence upon principle of personal responsibility would result in attacks on foreigners and foreign property by enemies of officials in power to discredit latter.
Would the Department assent to proposal of diplomatic body if limited to a term of years?
Ruddock

title: The Assistant Chief of the Division of the American Republics (Briggs) to the Ambassador in Cuba (Wright)

Dear Mr. Ambassador: Your message concerning a proposed settlement of the public works debt situation which would leave out of consideration the Purdy and Henderson group was passed on to Mr. Welles before his conversation with Senator Casanova yesterday afternoon. Mr. Welles stated that he would tell Senator Casanova that any settlement of the public works debt which did not include Purdy and Henderson would be considered an incomplete one and would not enable this Government to consider additional public works financing for Cuba.
Senator Casanova went on to New York almost immediately after his talk with Mr. Welles, but we expect to see him again next week.
Yours very truly,


Ellis O. Briggs

title: Memorandum by the Assistant Secretary of State (White)
body:
Mr. Jules Henry, Counselor of the French Embassy, called to ask whether we have recognized the present Government in El Salvador. I told him that we have not; that we are still awaiting further information regarding the situation down there, especially the part, if any, played by the Vice President, Mr. Martinez, in the revolution, in order to know whether or not he is debarred from recognition by the provisions of the Treaty of 1923. Mr. Henry said that the French Government of course would like to follow our lead and asked if I would let him know when we had determined upon our course of action. I told him I should be glad to do so.
F[rancis] W[hite]

title: CURRENT FOREIGN RELATIONS
body:
1. I HAVE DISCUSSED THE UTILITY OF CURRENT FOREIGN
RELATIONS (CFR) WITH SENIOR STAFF AT THIS POST
AND HAVE LEARNED THAT THOSE WHO DO SCAN IT REGULARLY (AND
NOT ALL DO) FIND IT OF ONLY MARGINAL VALUE.
I MYSELF AM FORCED TO AGREE WITH THAT CONCLUSION.
ALTHOUGH I INVARIABLY FIND ONE OR TWO ITEMS OF
INTEREST IN EACH EDITION, I DO NOT FIND THAT CFR
IN ITS PRESENT FORM PROVIDES ME WITH MUCH INSIGHT
INTO THE MAJOR CONCERNS WHICH SHAPE OUR POLICY IN
THE AREAS COVERED.
2. I AGREE THAT IN ITS PRESENT FORM CFR IS ESSENTIALLY
A WEEKLY NEWS REVIEW.  IF IT COULD SERVE THE PURPOSE
DESCRIBED IN REFTEL PARA 3 IT WOULD BE MOST USEFUL
TO THOSE OF US IN THE FIELD.  OTHERWISE, I DO NOT
THINK IT MERITS THE EFFORT INVOLVED AND WOULD
RECOMMEND ITS DISCONTINUANCE.
SHOESMITH

title: Mr. Seward to Mr. Adams.
body:
No. 720.]

Sir: The opening of the campaign is attended with some embarrassments which, in the excitement of the moment, are likely to be exaggerated. The expedition of General Franklin to Sabine Pass was only one of three designed to re-establish the national authority in Texas. Its repulse may retard, but it is not thought that it endangers, the success of the plan.
Official despatches from the army of the Cumberland have been received of a date so late as two o'clock p.m. of the 21st. They are inexplicit, but their general effect is thought to justify the expectation of our continuing to hold our important positions in Tennessee. Should any later news. be seasonably received, I will communicate it by telegraph.
I am, sir, your obedient servant,

WILLIAM H. SEWARD.
Charles Francis Adams, Esq., &c., &c., &c.
Same to ministers in Europe.

title: DETENTION OF ASSAD BUCARAM
body:
1. NEWSPAPERS HAVE REPORTED THE ARREST OF ASAAD BUCARAM,
LEADER OF THE CONCENTRATION DE FUERZAS POPULARES (CFP -
CONCENTRATION OF POPULAR FORCES), THE EVENING OF SEPT. 10
IN GUAYAQUIL. FEW DETAILS WERE PROVIDED BUT BUCARAM WAS
APPARENTLY ARRESTED BY ARMED SECURITY POLICE AS HE LEFT A
FUNCTION AT PARTY HEADQUARTERS.
2. ACCORDING TO PRESS ACCOUNTS POLICE ALSO ATTEMPTED TO
ARREST CARLOS CORNEJO ORBE (PROMINENT MEMBER OF THE
VELASQUISTA PARTY) AT HIS QUITO HOME. CORNEJO, WHO WAS
ONE OF THE EARLY SUPPORTERS OF THE UNSUCCESSFUL COUP,
IS APPARENTLY STILL IN HIDING.
3. COMMENT: THE CFP HAS THE LARGEST AND STRONGEST
POPULAR BASE OF THE ECUADOREAN POLITICAL PARTIES.
ALTHOUGH NO OFFICIAL EXPLANATION HAS FOLLOWED BUCARAM'S
ARREST, IT IS LIKELY A RESULT OF A STRONG CRITICISM HE
PUBLISHED OF THE RODRIGUEZ GOVERNMENT FOLLOWING THE COUP
ATTEMPT. THE EMBASSY HAS NO REASON TO BELIEVE THAT
BUCARAM WAS INVOLVED IN COUP PLOTTING.
BREWSTER

title: MORIN BURNS FINGERS
body:
1.  IN BRIEF INTERVIEW APPEARING IN AUGUST 31 MONTREAL
GAZETTE, MINISTER OF INTERGOVERNMENTAL AFFAIRS CLAUDE MORIN
DENIED THAT HE HAD EVER SUGGESTED ESTABLISHMENT OF A "PARLIAMENT"
BETWEEN A SOVEREIGN QUEBEC AND CANADA.  MORIN SAID THAT ORIGINAL
STORY IN HALIFX CHRONICLE-HERALD, IN WHICH HE DISCUSSED POSSIBILITY
OF SOME SORT OF COMMON BODY MADE UP OF REPRESENTATIVES OF
QUEBEC AND CANADA TO DEAL WITH MUTUAL PROBLEMS, WAS CORRECT.
BUT HE DENIED MENTIONING A "FEDERAL" OR "CENTRAL PARLIAMENT"
WITH AUTONOMOUS POWERS, AS SUBSEQUENT STORIES HAD SUGGESTED.
MORIN ADDED THAT ALL SUCH IDEAS WERE HYPOTHETICAL IN ANY CASE
AND WOULD HAVE TO BE DISCUSSED AFTER THE REFERENDUM.
2.  COMMENT:  ALARMED REACTION ON PART OF PQ MILITANTS HAS
PRESUMABLY REMINDED MORIN AND OTHERS IN GOQ OF THE DANGERS OF
THINKING OUT LOUD ABOUT VARIOUS ASSOCIATION OPTIONS.  LAUNCHING
OF TRIAL BALLOONS WITH HASTY DENIAL WHEN FACED WITH UNFAVORABLE
REACTION IS CLASSIC MORIN TACTIC.
MCNAMARA

title: Memorandum by the Assistant Chief of the Division of European Affairs (Hickerson)
body:
I have read and considered carefully the British reply to our protest of December 8 last against their interference with exports from Germany. A copy of the Embassy's telegram quoting this note is attached. I consider this note a combination of misstatements of international law and propaganda. It would be comparatively easy to draft a reply to this note taking issue with a number of their statements of law, but I do not believe that we would get anywhere; and I recommend that this note be filed without reply. I suggest that instead of replying to this note we press for favorable action in individual cases.
This being a British note, obviously we can take no action in the matter of making it public; if the British wish to make it public, they will of course do so.

J[ohn] D. H[ickerson]

title: The American Minister to Peru to the Secretary of State.
body:
[Telegram.]

 
Yesterday afternoon Minister for Foreign Affairs of Peru informed Mr. Alfonso [that] President of Peru accepted the proposal  of Chile for division of Tacna-Arica. Precise line and indemnity to be settled later by discussion. Chilean agent without credentials, but sent by President of Chile.
Minister for Foreign Affairs of Peru suggested the need of some mutually friendly nation to advise the arrangement in order to create favorable public opinion. Chilean agent proposed Great Britain, which was accepted. Minister for Foreign Affairs of Peru suggested, in view of the understanding, Chile put an end to the agitation in Ecuador and in Bolivia. title: Contacts with member countries: Burundi - Correspondence 01
body:
BIOGRAPHICAL NOTE
Mr. Terence Nsanze
Ambassador of the Republic of Burundi
Ambassador Terence Nsanze is 36 years old and has been living
in the United States since 1961. Until 1965, he was studying at
Georgetown, Howard, American and Columbia Universities. He graduated
in languages (English) and political science. In 1965, he was
appointed counselor to the Burundi permanent mission to the United
Nations. He became subsequently permanent representative and, in
May 1967, Ambassador of his country in Washington and Fewembe. 0774wWA ,
Burundi having been elected, at the last General Assembly of the
United Nations, a member of the Security Council, Ambassador Nsanze
chaired the Council in January. Mr. Nsanze has always been very
keen in following the Bank's current and future operations in his
country, particularly with respect to a possible power project
(see paragraph 12 of attached brief).

title: Mr. Seward to Mr. Dayton.
body:
No. 31.] 
Sir: * * * * * * * *
You will receive the account of a deplorable reverse of our arms at Manassas. For a week or two that event will elate the friends of the insurgents in Europe as it confounded and bewildered the friends of the Union here for two or three days. The shock, however, has passed away, producing no other results than a resolution stronger and deeper than ever to maintain the Union, and a prompt and effective augmentation of the forces for that end exceeding what would otherwise have been possible. The heart of the country is sound. Its temper is now more favorable to the counsels of deliberation and wisdom.
I am, sir, respectfully, your obedient servant,
WILLIAM H. SEWARD.
William L. Dayton, Esq., &c., &c., &c.

Baron Machio stated that, in its desire to avoid interference in the affairs of Latin American States, his Government was not inclined to probe too deeply into the methods by which their chief executives attained office and that, consequently, in the case of Mexico recognition would probably be accorded to whoever might succeed in establishing himself in power.

RECEIVED INSTRUCTIONS TO MAKE DEMARCHE AND OTHERS
AGREED TELEPHONE FOR INSTRUCTIONS.  FRENCHMAN DECIDED

MORNING.  AT ANY RATE, FRENCH AMBASSADOR NOW HAS GO
AHEAD AND CONFIRMS THAT APPROACH SHOULD BE MADE
TUESDAY AFTERNOON.

OR OF HOSTILE INTENT. QUOTING A SENIOR ISRAELI SOURCE,
THE STORS SAYS "WE SURMISE THE MOVE TO BE A
PURELY TECHNICAL ONE."

THAT ISRAEL CALLED FOR SPECIAL INSPECTION OF GOLAN
DISENGAGEMENT AREA ON DECEMBER 5 (IN
ADVANCE OF REGULARLY-SCHEDULED DEC. 6-7 INSPECTION).
RESULTS SHOWED FOLLOWING VIOLATIONS BY SYRIANS:
(A) 10 130 MM PIECES IN 10-KILOMETER ZONE.
(B) 3 SAM'S AND LAUNCHERS IN 20-KILOMETER ZONE AND
(C) 8 SAMS AND LAUNCHERS IN 25-KIOLOMETER ZONE.
3. UN SOURCE REFUSED TO SPECULATE ON REASONS FOR
SYRIAN VIOLATIONS.
NEWLIN

I await early reply.

138. Conversations have taken place between the Export-Import Bank, the Department and Ambassador Turbay regarding the Colombian request for additional credits. The Bank has already offered to increase the credit to $10,000,000 and the Department continues to press for $12,000,000. The matter should be clarified within a few days.
The Colombian request included 2 million Colombian pesos for the stabilization fund. The Department, the Export-Import Bank, and the Treasury believe that this is a proper matter for discussion with the Treasury Department, and Ambassador Turbay has been informed of this opinion. He has stated that he would consult his Government for instructions whether to proceed with stabilization discussions with the Treasury Department.
Hull

body:
305. Today's press carries news despatch from New York stating that it is learned from reliable sources that in view of the probability of war in Abyssinia the American Government has in principle decided to recall its diplomatic agent in Addis Ababa and make an explicit declaration of neutrality. It is also stated that in reply to pressure brought by anti-Italian elements on the ground of the resentment  of the Negro population a highly placed American official is alleged to have called attention to the equally strong potential resentment of the Italian population. The despatch concludes that unquestionably any anti-Italian action based on alleged American sympathies for the Abyssinians would provoke strong reaction from American-Italians who are following developments with "fervid patriotism".


Kirk

title: The Italian Embassy to the Department of State
body:
Aide Memoire
The International Conference for emigration and immigration to be held in Rome during the first months of 1924 is assuming  considerable importance on account of the large number of States that have accepted to participate.
In consideration of this it would perhaps be advisable to have a preliminary meeting of the experts of the Countries most interested in view of determining the technical questions to be discussed by the several sections of the Conference in Rome.
The meeting could take place in December or January in Genoa, Pallanza, Geneva or Ouchy.
The Italian Government would like to know if such a proposal would be agreeable to the Government of the United States and which date and locality would be considered most convenient.

title: ROMANIAN-SOUTH KOREAN RELATIONS

AT HIS REQUEST, POL COUNSELOR (TIPTON) GAVE HOUR-LONG
BRIEFING TO AMBASSADOR SUK CHAN LO, OF ROK GOVERNMENT
DELEGATION TO CURRENT RED CROSS CONFERENCE HERE.  PRINCIPAL
THEME WAS ROMANIAN-NORTH KOREA RELATIONS AND IMPLICATIONS
FOR ROK.  GENERAL CONCLUSION PRESENTED BY POL COUNSELOR
WAS THAT, GIVEN STRONG ROMANIAN-NORTH KOREAN ITES, ROK
OPPORTUNITIES WITH ROMANIA ARE EXTREMELY LIMITED AND
PROBABLY SUBJECT TO A KIND OF NORTH KOREAN VETO.  BEST
CHANCE FOR USEFUL CONTACTS IS IN SUCH MULTILATERAL CONTEXTS
AS UN AND PRESENT RED CROSS MEETING SINCE BILATERAL POSSI-
BILITIES WILL REMAIN ESSENTIALLY CLOSED FOR FORSEEABLE FUTURE.
AMBASSADOR SUK AGREED AND VOLUNTEERED THAT HE IS SEEKING
APPOINTMENT WITH ROMANIAN MFA DEPUTY DIRECTOR FOR INTERNATIONAL
ORGANIZATION AFFAIRS TO DISCUSS KOREA ISSUE AT UN AND
RELATED TOPICS.

title: The Secretary of State to Ambassador Guthrie
body:
[Telegram.]

 
Please call upon the Minister for Foreign Affairs and present to him a note textually as follows:
"In view of the circumstances of the negotiations which have taken place and which are now pending between the Government of Japan and the Government of China, and of the agreements which have been reached as a result thereof, the Government of the United States has the honor to notify the Imperial Japanese Government that it cannot recognize any agreement or undertaking which has been entered into or which may be entered into between the Governments of Japan and China, impairing the treaty rights of the United States and its citizens in China, the political or territorial integrity of the Republic of China, or the international policy relative to China commonly known as the open door policy.
"An identical note has been transmitted to the Government of the Chinese Republic."


Bryan.

title: Documentos referentes à atuação de Azeredo da Silveira, como ministro das Relações Exteriores, nas relações entre o Brasil e Portugal. O dossiê contém informações sobre a designação do general Dafontoura para o posto de embaixador brasileiro, em Portugal; a missão ao Brasil do primeiro-ministro português Carlos Galvão de Mello, em junho de 1974, após os aconteimentos político de 25 de Abril, que depôs o general Spínola; a viagem do titular à Lisboa, em dezembro de 1974, para acerto da agenda de conversações sobre acordos vigentes, entre os dois países, nas áreas comercial, de cooperação técnica, cultural, econômica e judiciária, além do estabelecimento de mecanismos de consultas bilaterais e de cooperação na ONU, principalmente, com relação à questão da descolonização da África portuguesa  e a relação do Brasil com esses países. Inclui ainda documentos sobre o asilo político do general Spínola e outros portugueses no Brasil, e de brasileiros em Portugal, entre os quais, Leonel Brizola, em outubro de 1977; sobre a imigração portuguesa; a visita ao Brasil do primeiro-ministro português Mário Soares, em dezembro de 1976; a independência dos Açores (1977); a denúncia pela Assembléia portuguesa da situação dos presos políticos brasileiros; e a visita do presidente português Ramalho Eanes, ao Brasil, em maio de 1978, para tratar da cooperação lusa-brasileira, na África.

title: ISRAELI AIR RAID ON BEIRUT
body:
1.  AT 1400 GMT, ACCORDING TO LEBANESE ARMY, G-2 FOUR
RPT FOUR ISRAELI PHANTOMS MADE AT LEAST TWO PASSES OVER
BEIRUT, LAUNCHING ROCKETS AGAINST TARGETS IN SABRA
QUARTER (WHICH INCLUDES SHATILA REFUGEE CAMP).  NO
INFO AS YET AVAILABLE ON DAMAGE AND CASUALTIES.
ATTACKS WERE MET BY ANTIAIRCRAFT FIRE, BUT NO HITS
WERE OBSERVED.  ISRAELI AIRCRAFT DEPARTED AFTER
APPROXIMATELY FIVE MINUTES.
2.  COMMENT:  WE APPRECIATE PROVOCATION FOR SOME
ISRAELI ACTION, BUT I MUST MAKE CLEAR THAT WE
CANNOT GUARANTEE SECURITY AMERICAN COMMUNITY OF SOME
6,000 PERSONS IN BEIRUT IF ISRAELIS ATTACK CITY.
WOULD HOPE DEPT. WILL TAKE MEASURES IMMEDIATELY TO ASSURE
THAT THERE IS NO RPT NO REPETITION OF RAIDS AGAINST
BEIRUT.  PRESUME DEPT. WOULD ALSO SEE FIT TO DEPLORE RAIDS
ON CROWDED POPULATION CENTERS.  WE ARE EXTREMELY
LUCKY TO GET OFF UNSCATHED IN APRIL 1973 ISRAELI RAID,
BUT WE CANNOT PUSH OUR LUCK TOO FAR.
HOUGHTON UNQTE INGERSOLL

CONTINUES TO BE UNSTABLE.  PRESENT NEGOTIATIONS OVER THE

BEEN SINGLED OUT AS TARGETS IN THIS SITUATION.  FYI ALL
VIP VISITS ARE DISCUSSED WITH SPANISH SECURITY FORCES TO
DETERMINE LEVEL OF ACTIVITY OF TERRORIST GROUPS AND ANY
POSSIBLE ACTIVITIES DIRECTED TOWARD VISITORS.  PERIOD OF
VISIT REFTEL HOLDS NO PARTICULAR SIGNIFICANCE AND SECURITY
PROBLEMS ARE NOT EXPECTED.  CHANGES IN SITUATION WILL BE
REPORTED IMMEDIATELY.  TODMAN

title: NIGERIA AS IMPORTER OF PETROLEUM PRODUCTS EMBASSY IS POUCHING AIRGRAM  WHICH SHOWS
body:
EMBASSY IS POUCHING AIRGRAM WHICH SHOWS
THAT, DESPITE ABUNDANT
CRUDE OIL, NIGERIA IS RAPIDLY BECOMING A SIGNIFICANT IMPORTER
OF PETROLEUM PRODUCTS. THE SINGLE REFINERY HAS REACHED MAXIMUM
OUTPUT, AND IMPORTS (CURRENTLY ABOUT 1.6 MILLION BARRELS PER YEAR
OR ABOUT TEN PERCENT OF CONSUMPTION) WILL NEARLY DOUBLE IN 1974
AND INCREASE EACH YEAR THEREAFTER (THOUGH WILL AT A DECLINING
RATE) UNTIL A SECOND REFINERY COMES ON STREAM (POSSIBLY IN 1977).
IRONICALLY, NIGERIA LIKE MOST OTHER COUNTRIES IS THEREFORE
VULNERABLE TO THE PROSPECT OF SHORTFALLS IN THE WORLD SUPPLY OF
REFINED PRODUCTS.

title: 159. Editorial Note
body:
The period of July to November 1957 was marked by slow and sporadic progress in the Azores base negotiations. Although Ambassador Bonbright had informed Secretary Dulles on August 28 that Prime Minister Salazar instructed Dr. Cunha to conclude the negotiations as soon as possible, the proceedings were hampered by Dr. Cunha's ill health, his preparation for his daughter's impending wedding, and difficulties in obtaining U.S. clearance for agreed positions. (Telegram 88 from Lisbon, August 28; telegram 50 from Lisbon, August 8; and telegram 158 from Lisbon, October 8; Department of State, Central Files, 711.56353B/8-2857, 711.56353B/8-857, and 711.56353B/10-857)
Changes in the wording of the text were agreed upon on November 8. (Telegram 216 from Lisbon, November 8; ibid., 711.56353B/11-857) The agreement, signed by representatives of both governments on November 15, extended until December 31, 1962. For text, see 8 UST (pt. 1) 409-412.

195. I have just learned that strenuous objections (behind the scenes, naturally) are being made by the Japanese to the United States joining in the Council's deliberations under any condition. Gilbert

title: LOS: 200-MILE ECONOMIC ZONE
body:
1. JAPANESE EMBASSY ACCRA HAS PICKED UP REPORT THAT GHANA
INTENDS DECLARE 200-MILE ECONOMIC ZONE IN COASTAL WATERS IN
JANUARY, 1975. ACCORDING THIS REPORT, GOG NOW PREPARING NECESSARY
DECREES, OFFICIAL STATEMENTS, AND PUBLIC RELATIONS MATERIAL TO
EXPLAIN MOVE. JAPANESE CLAIM TWO SEPARATE SOURCES THIS REPORT,
ONE IN STATE FISHING CORPORATION, THE OTHER IN GOVERNMENT
INFORMATION SERVICES DEPARTMENT. HOWEVER, REPORT RELAYED TO
JAPANESE EMBASSY FROM COMMERCIAL JAPANESE FISHING FIRMS OPERATING
IN GHANA. WHILE THEIR DIRECT INTEREST IN SUCH A MOVE MAKES THEM
SENSITIVE TO ANY INFO AVAILABLE, IT ALSO INCLINES THEM TO
EXAGGERATION OF POSSIBILITIES INTO CERTAINTIES.
2. THIS EMBASSY'S UNDERSTANDING HAS BEEN THAT GHANA IS
INTERESTED IN A 200-MILE ECONOMIC ZONE, BUT THAT IT WOULD MOST
LIKELY ONLY MAKE SUCH A MOVE IN CONCERT WITH OTHER COASTAL STATE
MEMBERS OF OAU. INFO ADDRESSEES MAY BE ABLE CONFIRM IF SUCH
OAU MOVEMENT DEVELOPING.
HANSON

title: The Secretary of State to the Ambassador in Cuba (Guggenheim)
body:
[Paraphrase]

129. Your 138, November 14, 10 a.m. While I fully appreciate your desire to be helpful in the present difficult political situation in Cuba, yet I am somewhat troubled at the implications involved in your taking any initiative in extending good offices between President Machado and the Opposition leaders, particularly in your saying anything to the Opposition which they might take as encouragement at this critical time. If President Machado asks your informal cooperation and help, the matter would have a somewhat different aspect. I think you should be very careful not to originate any move which might be interpreted as interfering either by the Government of the United States or by you personally in Cuban internal political affairs.
Stimson

body:
54. For Ambassador. Please deliver following message to Khru-shchev/Brezhnev from the President: 
"The American people are grateful for your message of good will on the anniversary of our Independence Day. The American Revolution was based on the desire of our people to build a free nation in a world of peace. Today, that desire for peace is more urgent than ever. The world has long passed that time when armed conflict can be the solution to international problems. That is why I share your desire, expressed in your message of today, that we move forward with understanding towards the solution of those key problems which divide us. I am hopeful that a world peace, just and lasting, can be achieved.
John F. Kennedy"

title: Editorial Note
body:
No. 94
 Italian Prime Minister De Gasperi and Foreign Minister Sforza arrived in London on March 12 for 3 days of talks with Prime Minister Attlee and Foreign Secretary Bevin. During these discussions, the British Government reaffirmed its support of the tripartite declaration of March 20, 1948, although it emphasized its desire that the matter be settled by conciliation between Italy and Yugoslavia. For a report on these talks by Ambassador Dunn, see telegram 4198 from Rome, Document 264. The official communique issued after the meetings is printed in Folliot, Documents on International Affairs, 1951, page 89.

title: VISIT OF THE IADB TO NICARAGUA
body:
1. FONSEC BRUTUS CALLED EMBASSY AFTER HAVING TALKED WITH
AMBASSADOR SALOMON IN WASHINGTON. HE STATED THAT
AMBASSADOR SALOMON SAID SOME LATIN AMERICAN REPRESENTATIVES
AT THE IADB WERE SUGGESTING THAT THE VISIT BE POSTPONED
FOR SECURITY REASONS. THE FONSEC SAID THAT IF A DECISION
TO POSTPONE THE IADB VISIT TO NICARAGUA WERE BASED ON
SUCH UNSUITABLE GROUNDS, THAT HAITI WOULD ABSTAIN. HAITI,
HE SAID, HAD HAD CONSIDERABLE INTERNAL PROBLEMS IN THE
MIDDLE '60'S YET HAD NEVERTHELESS CONTINUED TO RECEIVED
VISITS BY THE IADB AND OTHER GROUPS.
2. IN RESPONSE TO EMBASSY QUESTION, FONSEC INDICATED
THAT IF THERE WERE SOME MORE NEUTRAL WAY OF POSTPONING
THE VISIT, FOR EXAMPLE, ALONG THE LINES OF HIS SUGGESTION
CONCERNING THE POSTPONEMENT OF THE VISIT SO AS
NOT TO INTERFERE WITH THE MEDIATION TALKS, HAITI
WOULD VOTE FOR A POSTPONEMENT.
JONES

[Extract]

 
Mr. Blechingberg telephoned me this morning and said that he had at last received instructions from the Foreign Office in Copenhagen to leave the United States as soon as possible and to take Mr. Moller and Mr. Tscherning with him. title: 1. Editorial Note
body:
On February 20, 1969, President Richard M. Nixon sent a memorandum to Secretary of the Interior Walter Hickel that stated:
"A wide range of complex and highly important issues affecting the nation's oil import policies must be dealt with in the near future. These issues, which have not been examined in depth for a decade, are of such moment to the United States and their impact on national policy is so far-reaching that they require extensive review in detail and in the aggregate.
"I am therefore reassuming full responsibility for oil import policies--a responsibility delegated to the Department of the Interior some five years ago--so that there may be full opportunity for the several affected agencies efficiently to coordinate and assert their views.
"This undertaking will include a full review of the nation's oil import policies by the Executive Offices of the President." (Public Papers: Nixon, 1969, page 122)

Among these is the general treaty of peace and friendship signed in Washington on February  7, 1923, and still in effect as between Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua. The Government of Honduras in agreeing to the recognition trusts that Guatemala will comply fully and specifically with the terms of that treaty, so that the neutrality of Honduras shall be respected and its territory not violated under any conditions. Repeated to Guatemala.


Erwin

title: CROATIAN ATTACK ON FRG CONGEN CHICAGO
body:
REFERENCE:  STATE 209875
1.  AT TODAY'S PRESS CONFERENCE, ACTING FRG SPOKESMAN
GRUENEWALD MADE THE FOLLOWING STATEMENT ON THE CROATIAN
ATTACK ON THE FRG CONGEN IN CHICAGO:
BEGIN TEXT:  THE FEDERAL REPUBLIC WELCOMES THE
NON-VIOLENT END OF THE HOSTAGE TAKING.  IMMEDIATELY
AFTER LEARNING OF THE GOOD NEWS FROM CHICAGO, FOREIGN
MINISTER GENSCHER, IN HIS OWN NAME AS WELL AS THAT OF
THE CHANCELLOR, THANKED SECRETARY OF STATE VANCE FOR THE
PRUDENT ACTION OF THE AMERICAN AUTHORITIES, WHICH MADE
POSSIBLE THIS HAPPY OUTCOME.  DURING THE CONVERSATION,
SECRETARY VANCE PRAISED THE CLOSE COOPERATION BETWEEN
AMERICAN AND GERMAN AUTHORITIES.  VANCE SAW IN THIS
COOPERATION A NEW INDICATION OF THE GOOD AND FRIENDLY
RELATIONS BETWEEN THE US AND THE FEDERAL REPUBLIC.  END
TEXT.
2.  GRUENEWALD STRESSED, DURING THE Q AND A SESSION,
THAT THE FRG HAD NOT MADE ANY PROMISES TO THE TERRORISTS.
MEEHAN

title: The Peruvian Legation to the Department of State
body:
Memorandum
The Minister of Peru is instructed to advise The Honourable The Secretary of State that the Government of Peru accepts the mediation of the President of the United States, and that the President of Peru will shortly communicate this acceptance by cable in reply to the message of the President of the United States.
The Government of Peru, however, does not desire that the mediation should assume the character of an American Continental mediation.
It has accepted the mediation of the President of the United States, because the Government of Peru considers the President of the United States to be the initiator and the supporter of those principles which are to be asserted at the general Peace Conference.

14. The Department would appreciate receiving from you as soon as you can prepare it a telegram somewhat along the following lines, but in greater factual detail.
Since Bohemia and Moravia have been occupied by Germany which has declared a protectorate and sent military officials to assume the functions of government; since Slovakia, through her President, has asked Hitler to assume a protectorate, and since Ruthenia is now occupied by Hungarian troops, there are no Czechoslovak officials with whom you can carry on business. In the circumstances you request instructions as to your future activities.
Upon receipt of such a telegram we shall reply directing you to close the Legation and turn over the files and archives to the Consul General, and to return to Washington at your convenience.
Your telegram should be drafted in such form that if we desire it can be given publicity.


Welles

title: Memorandum by Mr. Landreth M. Harrison of the Division of Eastern European A fairs
body:
Our counter-proposals were made known to the Minister of Finland on December 12, 1935. The Minister, after studying the working draft of the counter-proposals, sent Dr. von Numers, Secretary of the Legation, to the Division of Eastern European Affairs to arrange with me  a cable to the Finnish Foreign Office setting forth our counter-proposals with respect to Schedules I and II. Such a cable was drafted and sent on December 13. The Minister was then furnished with three copies of the attached schedules. Two copies were to be sent immediately by mail to Finland and the third to be retained in the Legation's files. The Minister stated that he should shortly receive from Helsingfors his Government's reaction to the counter-proposals.
L. M. Harrison

title: RESIGNATION OF CHIANG YEN-SHIH
body:
REFERENCE: TAIPEI 2239
WE RECALL THAT THE EMBASSY LAST YEAR IDENTIFIED CHIANG
YEN-SHIH AS A POSSIBLE CARETAKER SUC-

title: Executive Order No. 2770, December 7, 1917, Supplemental to Executive Order of October 12, 1917
body:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by "An Act to Define, Regulate and Punish Trading with the Enemy and for Other Purposes", approved October 6, 1917, I hereby make the following orders, rules and regulations: 
 I hereby prohibit any and all foreign insurance companies from doing business within the United States after February 1, 1918, unless such companies shall first obtain from the Secretary of the Treasury licenses to do business.
 I further hereby vest in the Secretary of the Treasury the power and authority to issue at any time, upon such terms and conditions as the Secretary of the Treasury may deem proper and as are not inconsistent with law, or to refuse, a license to any foreign insurance company to do business within the United States through agencies, branch offices or otherwise.





Woodrow Wilson

body:
[Telegram.]

Monday several hundred Armenians marched on the Porte professedly to ask redress of grievances. The patriarch tried to prevent it. A conflict occurred between Armenians and police. Probably about 60 Turks and Armenians killed--among others Turkish major--and many wounded. Armenians carried pistols. Yesterday several more were killed. Last night 80 killed. Several hundred imprisoned. Porte had notice of the demonstration, which they say was organized by leaders of Huntchaguist revolutionists, whom they have captured. Much terror exists. I think Porte will be able to restrain fanaticism.


Terrell.

title: Memorandum of the Assistant Secretary of State ( Phillips) to the Secretary of State
body:
Dear Mr. Secretary: Mr. de Laboulaye called this afternoon in behalf of the French Ambassador and expressed the Ambassador's regret that he could not call himself upon you to-day. The Embassy has received an urgent telegram from Paris saying that the British and French Governments are prepared jointly to address the Japanese Government with the request that Japan should send troops to the west front next spring and summer. The French regard this of the highest importance, but do not wish to take any further step in the matter until they are assured that there will be no objection raised by the Government of the United States.

Sincerely,



W. Phillips

title: Sir Julian Pauneefote to Mr. Blaine.
body:
Sir: I have the honor to inform you that after our interview on the 13th instant on the subject of the course to be adopted with reference to the conduct of the chief justice of Samoa in absenting himself without leave, I telegraphed to the Marquis of Salisbury your suggestion that the chief justice be called upon for an explanation by the three consuls at Samoa by order of their respective governments instead of through the King of Sweden.
I have now received a telegram from his lordship in reply, stating that this suggestion has been accepted by Her Majesty's Government and that of Germany, and informing me at the same time that Her Majesty's consul at Samoa has been instructed by telegraph to concert with his colleagues a joint note to the chief justice.
I have, etc.,
Julian Pauncefote.

title: The Ambassador in Italy (Phillips) to the Secretary of State
body:
20. I am informed by the British Ambassador in strictest confidence that he was summoned on Saturday by Ciano and informed that the Italian Government was holding 60 battalions of troops in readiness to send to Spain if France should take any steps to intervene on behalf of Negrin Government. The Ambassador immediately communicated this information to his Government which forwarded it without comment to Paris before the recent meeting of the Council of Ministers. In addition to the anti-French press campaign reported in my 19, January 17, 7 p.m., this was obviously intended by the Italians to bring further pressure on the French.
According to the best information available in Rome the decision of the French Council not to intervene has apparently eliminated any  immediate danger since it does not appear that the Italians will take action to support Franco unless other powers intervene on the other side.
Phillips

title: 260. Telegram From the Station in Iran to the Central Intelligence Agency
body:
TEHE 686. 1. Al Homdulillah.
2. Late last night, accompanied by kisses (literally) from Iranian source, we informed papers brought by [name not declassified]. They now in possession Zahedi. Evidently pressure finally effective and we feel much credit must go to [name not declassified]. Action scheduled midnight tonight.
3. Earlier meeting with Zahedi showed him firm of purpose but inhabiting dream world so far as his subsequent program concerned.  Spoke of free medical care for the third class citizens, mechanizing agriculture and growing vast crops of cotton on Moghan Steppes, equalizing wealth by income taxes, etc. Time not right for us to argue issue but we warning strongly against making impossible promises in early speeches. It clear Zahedi will need firm realistic guidance.
End of message.

1. IN PARA NINE REFTEL COL. QADHAFI INDICATED TO JACK
ANDERSON THAT ONE REASON LIBYA IS RELUCTANT TO SELL C-130'S

title: HUMAN RIGHTS: ALEXANDRA JOHNSON
body:
1.  WASHINGTON STAR STORY TODAY CONTAINS FOLLOWING PARA-
GRAPH.
2.  BEGIN TEXT.  "JOHNSON WAS SUSPECTED BY THE SHIN BEIT
OF AIDING TERRORIST CELLS THERE.  SHE REPORTEDLY WAS FOL-
LOWED FOR ALMOST THREE YEARS BY ISRAELI SECRET AGENTS AND
HER TELEPHONE IN JERUSALEM WAS TAPPED.
THIS WAS CARRIED OUT IN COORDINATION WITH THE FBI.  PER-
MISSION TO FOLLOW HER AND TO TAP HER TELEPHONE WAS REQUESTED
ABOUT SIX MONTHS AFTER JOHNSON ARRIVED IN JERUSALEM, BUT
BECAUSE OF HER DIPLOMATIC STATUS, THE SHIN BEIT DID NOT ACT
UNTIL THE FBI AGENT STATIONED AT THE U.S. EMBASSY IN TEL
AVIV APPROVED."  END TEXT.
3.  ALLEGATION WAS BROUGHT UP BY QUESTIONER IN NOON BRIEF-
ING BUT SPOKESMAN DID NOT RESPOND DIRECTLY TO IT.  WE WILL
BE WORKING UP GUIDANCE ON THIS AND PROVIDE IT WHEN READY.
VANCE

body:

DECEMBER 20, AND IT SEEMED CLEAR THAT THE TROOPS

UNSTUCK, AND THIS MAY BE IN PROCESS NOW.

title: TRAINING OF CAMEROONIAN AIR FORCE PILOTS IN WEST GERMANY

THE CAMEROONIAN MINISTRY OF THE ARMED FORCES RECENTLY REQUESTED
THAT THE WEST GERMAN AIR FORCE INCREASE THE NUMBER OF CAMEROONIAN

GERMAN AIR FORCE TO TRAIN APPROXIMATELY 20 CAMEROONIAN

BY BOTH COUNTRIES.

ADMINISTRATION OF THE PROJECT.STABLER

2476. Soviet press coverage formation Chinese Central People's Government totals 9 columns. Full page occupied Peking Tass despatch based Hsinhua [radio] transmitting general program People's Political Consultative Council.

Full translations above items being despatched.

title: MASSACRE OF VIETNAMESE REFUGEES OFF CAMBODIAN COAST
body:

RELATIVES REMAINING IN VIET-NAM VISITED LAEM SING BOAT CAMP
IN CHANTHABURI PROVINCE EARLY THIS WEEK. THERE THEY ENCOUNTERED
GROUP OF 20-24 REFUGEES WHO DEPARTED HA TIEN IN MID-OCTOBER
IN A SMALL BOAT WHICH WAS SLOWEST IN GROUP OF SIX DEPARTING
AT SAME TIME. AS THEIR BOAT WAS FOLLOWING CAMBODIAN COAST WITH
THE OTHERS WELL OUT IN FRONT, PASSENGERS BEGAN OBSERVING
VIETNAMESE BODIES IN WATER, SOME WITH THROATS SLIT. AT ONE
POINT THEY PASSED ONE OF THE SIX BOATS CONTAINING THREE BODIES,
ALL WITH THROATS CUT. THEY HURRIED PAST IT, DISCOVERING WHEN
THEY FINALLY REACHED THAILAND THAT NONE OF THE OTHER BOATS HAD
ARRIVED.
2. REFUGEES ASSUME THAT CAMBODIANS MASSACRED ALL THE PEOPLE
ON THE OTHER FIVE BOATS OR THAT SOME DROWNED AFTER
JUMPING OVERBOARD, ALTHOUGH THEY SAW NO CAMBODIANS. INFOR-
MATION CORRESPONDS WITH THAT REPORTED REFTEL, WHICH EMBASSY

title: The Minister in Poland (Gibson) to the Acting Secretary of State
body:
36. Department's 17, May 28, 6 p.m., received this evening.
Since my arrival in Poland I have endeavored to inform myself fully as to the treatment of Jews but possess no evidence which  would warrant charges referred to in Department's telegram or afford me any data to start specific investigations, therefore I should be glad to have Department furnish me a definite list of places where these events occurred, a statement of the charges made, the events in each place and if possible names of victims and of possible witnesses. If Department approves, I am then prepared to ask Doctor Bogen, director of the Jewish Joint Distribution Committee for Poland, and Lieutenant Colonel Bailey of the Red Cross to accompany me and make careful personal investigation in the various places. See my number 35.
[Gibson]

title: Documentos referentes às relações políticas, econômicas e comerciais entre Brasil e Estados Unidos no período em que Azeredo da Silveira era ministro das Relações Exteriores. O dossiê é constituído de relatórios, notas, discursos, resumos e correspondência, abordando, no âmbito das relações econômicas, a questão da exportação de calçados brasileiros ao mercado norte-americano; a discussão da criação de um grupo consultivo informal Brasil-EUA sobre assuntos econômicos; as questões referentes ao intercâmbio comercial, incluindo as negociações do Acordo Geral de Tarifas e Comércio (GATT), e a lei de comércio norte-americana promulgada em 1975, e que causou polêmica em países da América Latina por desrespeitar acordos firmados anteriormente sobre protecionismo. No âmbito das relações políticas, o dossiê inclui informações relativas ao grupo consultivo Brasil-EUA sobre cooperação científica e tecnológica; sobre a visita de Azeredo da Silveira a Washington, em outubro de 1976; e sobre o projeto e assinatura do Memorandum de Entendimento referente a consultas sobre assuntos de interesse mútuo entre Brasil-EUA. No âmbito dos direitos humanos, inclui informações sobre a prisão política de cidadãos americanos no Brasil, sobre a lei norte-americana de ajuda externa, no campo de segurança e assistência militar; e sobre a denúncia feita pelo governo brasileiro em 1977, do acordo militar Brasil-EUA de 1952.

title: CHOLERA STATUS REPORT
body:
IN THE TWO WEEK PERIOD, JULY 12-25, ACCORDING TO OFFICIAL
PORTUGUESE SOURCES, CONFIRMED CHOLERA CASES IN CONTINENTAL
PORTUGAL ROSE BY 202.  OF THIS FIGURE, 100 CASES WERE FROM
OPORTO DISTRICT AND 59 FROM LISBON DISTRICT.  THERE WERE
ALSO 8 CHOLERA DEATHS DURING THIS PERIOD.  THEREFORE,
SINCE THE ONSET OF THE DISEASE LAST APRIL 24, THERE HAVE
BEEN A TOTAL OF 645 CONFIRMED CASES AND 18 DEATHS.
ALTHOUGH VACCINATION IS NOT OBLIGATORY FOR AMERICANS ENTERING
PORTUGAL OR RETURNING UT U.S., ITALIAN AUTHORITIES REQUIRE
VACCINATION FOR ALL VISITORS ARRIVING FROM PORTUGAL.

title: NEW BULGARIAN AMBASSADOR TO ROMANIA
body:
1.  BULGARIAN GOVERNMENT ANNOUNCED JULY 28 APPOINTMENT
OF FORMER MINISTER OF POWER SUPPLY PETUR DANAILOV AS
NEW AMBASSADOR TO ROMANIA, REPLACING IVAN STEFANOV
ABDAZHIEV, IN BUCHAREST SINCE 1974.  BULGARIAN PRESS
REPORTED JULY 30 PRESENTATION OF CREDENTIALS BY
DANAILOV IN BUCHAREST.

COOPERATION BETWEEN TWO COUNTRIES IN FIELD OF ENERGY.
FOR DANAILOV, IT MAY BE A DEMOTION, AFTER HAVING BEEN
A MINISTER SINCE 1973 ALTHOUGH HE WAS RE-ELECTED FULL
MEMBER OF CENTRAL COMMITTEE OF BCP AT ELEVENTH PARTY
CONGRESS.
3.  NO NEW POSITION HAS YET BEEN ANNOUNCED FOR
ABADZHIEV, WHO WAS DROPPED FROM BCP CENTRAL COMMITTEE
AT ELEVENTH CONGRESS.  ABADZHIEV WAS AT ONE TIME
YOUNGEST MEMBER OF POLITBURO AND REGARDED AS COMER
IN PARTY, PARTICULARLY AFTER HE CARRIED OUT PURGE
OF ANTI-ZHIVKOV ELEMENTS IN VRATSA DISTRICT
FOLLOWING 1965 COUP ATTEMPT.
4.  DEPARTMENT MAY WISH TO PROVIDE BUCHAREST WITH

MONTHS AND NOTHING HAPPENED BUT THIS TIME SITUATION "VERY, VERY
SERIOUS."  ABDO SAID CHRISTIAN MILITIA MAINLY KATAEB WITH FEW
PNL AND GUARDIANS OF CEDARS COOPERATING.  ABDO HAD JUST
